rules: Unresolved is a first-class result; "no trout" is a strong exclusion claim requiring scoped positive evidence.
Warmwater focus is a positive claim and may coexist with seasonal trout.
A reservoir is a trout fishery, not a trout stream; lake arms/depth never inherit tailwater evidence.
A stocking schedule is a plan; the recent-release report is a rolling window; a GIS point is neither.
Designations (TS/NRTS) are legal boundaries, never a fish census.

priorLeads.segment: The Barren Fork River, Warren County, flowing through McMinnville to its confluence with the Collins River just north of McMinnville (the Barren Fork lies inside the Collins HUC-8 05130107). TWRA's stocked reach is the Warren County main stem; the cataloged North Prong Barren Fork is cataloged separately (north-prong-barren-fork).
priorLeads.boundaries: Warren County main stem through McMinnville; HUC 05130107. Temperature evidence: TDEC stations at river-miles 4.4, 15.2, and 16.4 (35.63-35.68 N, the McMinnville reach) and USGS 03420500 near Trousdale.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No cold-water source documented. Catalog describes a gentle-gradient rain-driven river through McMinnville - no dam, no spring source cited by any agency.

holdover.detail: No agency documentation of holdover either way. TWRA's stocking is seasonal (three 2026 weeks: 3/15, 3/22, 5/10, Rainbow Trout); no summer/winter stocking rows and no creel or sampling evidence of between-stocking survival were found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented: the Barren Fork appears in NO TWRA trout category - the wild-trout list and every other trout designation on TWRA's trout regulations page exclude it (checked live this session), so the agency trout record here is stocking-based put-and-take rainbow only. (Wave-2's audit 'wild-trout candidate' flag was refuted at page level; a stocking program is not a wild-trout designation.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC's 2007-2008 sampling on the McMinnville reach shows summer water of 20-26.8 C (26.8 C in Aug 2007 at river-mile 4.4) and TWRA stocks the Barren Fork only in three spring weeks - seasonal put-and-take rainbow with no documented between-stocking survival.

priorLeads.segment: Beaverdam Creek, Johnson County — northeast Tennessee spring-creek-character creek in the Watauga HUC (06010102, South Fork Holston basin), flowing through Cherokee National Forest country toward the Virginia line near Damascus. TWRA Region IV report treats it as an annually monitored wild trout stream.
priorLeads.boundaries: Wild-trout water: 'Beaverdam Creek and tributaries from its confluence with Birch Branch downstream to Tank Hollow' (TWRA special trout regulations, wild trout streams table) — 5 trout/day, no length limit, single-hook artificials only. Reaches outside that designation: statewide trout rules. TWRA 2026 stocking schedule lists seasonal rainbow stocking weeks 3/1-6/21/2026 (every 4 weeks).

coldSourceSummary.notes: Catalog calls it a spring creek but no agency text confirming spring influence was found. Elevation context from TWRA Trout Management Plan: a 2006 qualitative survey of Green Mountain Branch (a Beaverdam Creek tributary) found a relatively abundant wild Rainbow Trout population at 3,080 ft elevation along Hwy 421 (https://digitalcommons.memphis.edu/govpubs-tn-wra-strategic-management-plans/10).

holdover.detail: No holdover-specific evidence found. Decisive currency is the documented resident wild trout population (below); TWRA 2026 seasonal rainbow stocking (Mar-Jun) coexists with the wild fishery.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2018: 'Beaverdam Creek is one of Tennessee's best-known wild trout streams and is on an annual monitoring schedule' — monitored since 1991 with primary species RBT/BNT; qualitative surveys found RBT and BNT at mainstem sites. Brook trout documented in Beaverdam Creek tributaries (Birch Branch listed among sympatric Brook/Rainbow waters; East Fork Beaverdam Creek listed as a potential native Brook Trout donor stream) — tributary evidence, not mainstem. TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 names Beaverdam Creek among former degraded streams that now 'provide excellent wild trout fisheries'.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA itself calls Beaverdam Creek one of Tennessee's best-known wild trout streams, annually monitored since 1991 for resident rainbow and brown trout — a self-sustaining population in a designated wild-trout water.

sourcesChecked: https://johnsoncitypress.com/news/2166/the-reel-thing-trout-fishing-to-pick-up-with-cooler-weather (newspaper lead, supports TWRA wild-brown sampling note; not cited as sole evidence)

meanings: winter put-and-take on a warm water (cold-month recruitment program)

priorLeads.segment: Beech Lake (USGS/TVA 'Beech Reservoir') on the Beech River at Lexington, Henderson County, West Tennessee. TWRA Region 1 winter put-and-take trout lake (catalog: seasonMonths Nov-Mar) over a warmwater bass/bream/catfish fishery; one of the 'Beech River Watershed Lakes' group in TWRA's regulation exceptions.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire lake. TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule lists 'Beech Lake' as a Winter-type Rainbow Trout site (repo workbook rows: Henderson Co., 1/14/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the schedule page renders dates 1/13/2026 and 2/10/2026 adjacent to the Beech Lake entry). No trout stockings of any other type found for the lake.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Dam identity basis: USGS inactive station 03594413 is named 'BEECH LAKE NEAR LEXINGTON, TENN (TVA)' (Henderson Co., HUC 06040001 Lower Tennessee-Beech, 35.66118,-88.41727). TVA's 'Beech Reservoir' page (tva.com, verified via WebSearch snippet only — tva.com blocks plain fetch) describes flood-storage of 4,430 acre-feet, ~3.65 miles long, and Beech Dam as a non-hydro dam; a WebSearch synthesis adds the dam was built early 1960s for water supply/flood control/recreation. No cold-release (deep-draw) regime documented; no evidence the lake receives or needs cold dam water.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover evidence found. Program design is winter put-and-take: the only trout rows for Beech Lake in TWRA's 2026 schedule are Winter-type, and the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 states hatchery-supported streams and lakes 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'. Warmwater stockings (bluegill/redear) also appear for the lake in TWRA's warmwater stocking archive.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented. The Trout Management Plan states wild trout are generally limited to East Tennessee's mountain streams; no wild-trout listing or record exists for this West Tennessee reservoir.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Winter put-and-take only: TWRA's 2026 schedule carries Beech Lake (Henderson Co.) solely as a Winter rainbow site, and the Trout Management Plan states hatchery-supported lakes like this are warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round.

catalogFields.notes: Regional Tennessee River tributary in Henderson and Decatur counties, distinct from nearby Beech Lake.

priorLeads.segment: Beech River main stem — a warmwater West Tennessee stream in Henderson and Decatur counties (USGS county codes 077 and 039), HUC8 06040001 (Lower Tennessee basin), draining east-central West Tennessee toward the Tennessee River/Kentucky Lake reach. USGS lists 8 Beech River gaging sites, all discontinued (several TVA-era); the furthest downstream is 03594484 'BEECH RIVER NEAR DECATURVILLE, TN' (251 sq mi drainage area). Distinct from nearby Beech Lake, a warmwater flood-control/water-supply reservoir in the Beech River watershed cluster that DOES receive TWRA winter rainbow stockings.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog gives no reach limits; record covers the Henderson County headwater reach near Lexington downstream through Decatur County near Decaturville. No trout program exists on the river itself.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Gage datum 428.83 ft (NGVD29) at discontinued USGS 03594415 'BEECH RIVER NEAR LEXINGTON TENN (TVA)' — lowland West TN elevation; no active USGS gage remains on the river (waterservices site service, checked 2026-09-18).

holdover.detail: No trout stocking program exists on the Beech River: TWRA's 2026 schedule (and the owner-supplied workbook grep) contains no 'Beech River' rows — only neighboring 'Beech Lake' (Henderson Co.) shows Region 1 Winter rainbow rows (1/14/2026, TBD 12/2026). With no stockings, holdover is not a documented facet of this water.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation. The TWRA Trout Management Plan states 'Wild trout are generally limited to East Tennessee's mountain streams'; the Beech River is a lowland West Tennessee warmwater tributary.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Control-style warmwater record: TWRA's stocking schedule has no Beech River trout rows at all, the Trout Management Plan places wild trout only in East Tennessee mountains, and no USGS temperature or coldwater habitat evidence exists for this lowland (~429 ft) stream.

catalogFields.notes: Major Maury County tributary in the Duck River basin and a locally significant general-fishing water.

priorLeads.segment: Big Bigby Creek (GNIS 01305201, HUC-8 06040003), the major west-bank Duck River tributary draining Maury County through the Columbia area - NOT Little Bigby Creek (separate GNIS water, TDECWPC-LBIGB004.1MY) and NOT the stocked McCutcheon Creek winter-trout water in Columbia. Agency monitoring spans the whole creek: USGS 03601500 'AT CROSS BRIDGES' (upper), USGS 03601100 'AT NEEDMORE' (middle), USGS 03600500 'AT SANDY HOOK' (lower), and TDECWPC-BBIGB008.5MY / 014.0MY / 016.3MY river-mile stations.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog: 'Major Maury County tributary in the Duck River basin' - full course within Maury County from the Cross Bridges headwater country to the Duck River confluence below Columbia (NHD reachcodes 06040003xxxx).

coldSourceSummary.notes: Un-dammed Western Highland Rim agricultural/residential creek. Four agency stations over four decades record June-September water temperatures of 20.5-31.0 C - no cold-water mechanism exists in the record.

holdover.detail: No trout presence of any kind is documented, so no holdover question arises. TWRA has never stocked this creek: the 2026 row-level schedule contains zero Bigby rows (the only trout rows in Maury County are McCutcheon Creek winter stockings), and the Trout MASTER layer returns zero Bigby sites.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found; TWRA's trout regulations page (fetched 2026-09-18) contains zero Bigby entries - no special regulation, no wild-trout listing.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Four agency stations (USGS 03600500/03601100/03601500 + TDECWPC-BBIGB008.5MY) record 20.5-31.0 C June-September temperatures across 1966-2008, and no trout stocking, regulation, or occurrence is documented for the creek anywhere.

priorLeads.segment: Big Rock Creek, Marshall County, Tennessee (catalog) — a small Duck River tributary through Lewisburg, rising in southwest Marshall County and flowing north about 20 river miles to its confluence with the Duck River (TDEC's nearest mainstem station is described as 'HIGHWAY 272 DOWNSTEAM BIG ROCK CREEK' at 35.577, -86.779, HUC 06040002). Catalog YAML carries no counties field; identity resolved from the catalog hydroIdentity (GNIS 01305230, HUC8 06040002) and confirmed against WQP station metadata: every 'Big Rock Creek' station found sits in HUC 06040002 with county code 117 (Marshall), matching the catalog note 'TWRA winter-stocked Marshall County creek near Lewisburg'. Same-named Big Rock Creeks elsewhere in Tennessee were not an issue here — all stations returned by the Marshall County sweep belong to this creek.
priorLeads.boundaries: The named Big Rock Creek within Marshall County (HUC 06040002); identity stations USGS-03599000 'BIG ROCK CREEK AT LEWISBURG, TN' (24.9 sq mi, alt 705.01 ft NGVD29) and USGS-03599100 'BIG ROCK CR AT DOUBLE BRIDGES, TN' (48.7 sq mi, alt 644.37 ft). TWRA's stocking-site string is 'Big Rock Greenway' (Region 2, Marshall) with no reach detail; the greenway lies along the creek in Lewisburg, so in-town gauge USGS-03599000 is the nearest temperature station to the stocking site.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Elevation 705.01 ft is the USGS-03599000 station altitude at Lewisburg (NGVD29); the downstream Double Bridges station sits at 644.37 ft — a low-relief agricultural/urban Marshall County valley with no gorge or canopy documentation found. No cold-water source of any kind documented. TDEC station TDECWPC-BROCK006.0ML is described as '100 YARDS DOWNSTREAM DAM AT VERONA', evidencing an unnamed small dam on the creek at Verona; no operator or release documentation exists, and the 26.3 deg C July 2000 grab below it shows no cold-release effect. Identity verified from WQP station metadata columns (station names, Marshall County code 117, HUC 06040002) because the USGS identity endpoint has been 503ing this week.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found. The TWRA program is winter-only catchable rainbows at 'Big Rock Greenway': 2026 workbook rows (Region 2, Marshall, type Winter, Rainbow Trout) are 1/15/2026, 2/27/2026 and TBD 12/2026; the live TWRA stocking page contains the 'Big Rock Greenway' site string (fetched copy's flattened table interleaves two tables, so its stray date cells cannot be attributed). No source documents survival between stockings or through summer, and the in-town summer record (USGS-03599000 nearest the greenway: 24.7-32.0 deg C June-September grabs) makes summer survival implausible on the cited temperatures alone.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation found in any agency source for Big Rock Creek. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Tennessee's wild trout in East Tennessee and describes hatchery-supported streams and lakes as 'primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' (canon quote; PDF not fetched per rule).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: 91 June-September grab samples across 1966-2025 on every reach of Big Rock Creek run 18.5-32.0 deg C — 25.3-32.0 deg C at the in-town Lewisburg gauge nearest the Big Rock Greenway stocking site — far above year-round trout survival thresholds.

catalogFields.notes: Major northwest Tennessee tributary entering Kentucky Lake near Big Sandy; a principal regional fishing river.

priorLeads.segment: Big Sandy River — West Tennessee tributary of the Tennessee River draining Henry, Benton, Carroll, and Henderson counties through the Big Sandy embayment into Kentucky Lake. TWRA names Big Sandy one of the 'three major river embayments' of Kentucky Reservoir (with Duck and Beech rivers). Warmwater bottomland river; no trout program exists anywhere on it.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog covers the whole river to its Kentucky Lake confluence near Big Sandy, TN (hydroIdentity GNIS 01277382, HUC8 06040005). TWRA's Big Sandy WMA (2,370 acres, Benton and Henry counties) protects riverbottom hardwoods, croplands, and swamps along the river; the Big Sandy Unit of Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge lies on the same peninsula between the river and the Tennessee River.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented: the river appears nowhere on TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule (full scan of the 616-row workbook — no 'Big Sandy' trout row of any type), it is absent from TWRA's warmwater stocking archive as well, and the TWRA Trout Management Plan places wild trout in East Tennessee mountain streams with no West Tennessee mention.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. The documented riparian context is lowland and warm: TWRA's Big Sandy WMA page (via WebSearch snippet; direct fetch of the page 404'd) describes riverbottom hardwoods, croplands, and swamps following the Big Sandy River in Benton and Henry counties; TWRA's Kentucky Reservoir page treats the Big Sandy embayment as warmwater (dewatering-area crappie rules; adjacent West Sandy/Big Sandy waterfowl closures).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Warm bottomland West Tennessee tributary: TWRA stocks no trout anywhere on the river (absent from both trout and warmwater stocking archives), it drains swampy riverbottom lowlands into the Kentucky Lake embayment, and no cold-water source is documented.

priorLeads.segment: Big Soddy Creek (locally 'Soddy Creek'), Hamilton County, draining the Soddy Creek Gorge country on Walden Ridge into Chickamauga Lake at Soddy-Daisy (Tennessee River HUC 06020001). TWRA stocks rainbow trout with a Seasonal (spring) program plus a Delayed-Harvest reach; the DH regulations define the special-regulation water as 'Big Soddy Creek: Upstream of Back Valley Road.'
priorLeads.boundaries: TWRA Delayed-Harvest reach: upstream of Back Valley Road (C&R season Nov 1 - Feb 28). USGS temperature record is at the lower creek (03566400 'SODDY CREEK AT SODDY' near the US-27 corridor/lake arm) and speaks to the lower reach, not the gorge DH reach.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Creek drains the Soddy Creek Gorge / Cumberland Trail section on the Walden Ridge escarpment above Soddy-Daisy, but no agency-published elevation or gorge microclimate figure was located. No creek-specific mining/AMD water-quality report was found: the closest peer-reviewed coal-drainage literature covers neighboring North Chickamauga Creek (OSTI 20727845, pH 3.6 fishless AMD zone), not Big Soddy - no impact is inferred here.

holdover.detail: No holdover study or creel evidence found. The Delayed-Harvest design (stockings in late Oct and Nov, catch-and-release Nov 1 - Feb 28 upstream of Back Valley Road, harvest reopening March) keeps stocked rainbows in the creek through winter by program design, but no agency documentation of trout carrying over into the following summer exists.

wildPopulation.detail: Not on TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list - the creek's only trout regulation entry is the Delayed-Harvest reach (upstream of Back Valley Road); no wild trout survey or self-sustaining population documentation found.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Historic USGS grabs at the lower creek (03566400) hit 33 C in July 1980 and 27 C in September 1979, and the fishery is exactly the seasonal-plus-DH rainbow put-and-take design the TWRA Trout Management Plan describes as warmwater habitat that 'cannot support trout year round'.

catalogFields.notes:
TVA reservoir on the South Fork Holston River northeast of Johnson City (Sullivan/Washington counties), impounded by Boone Dam (USGS 03486810, 36.44066/-82.43792). Two arms: the South Fork Holston arm fed by the South Holston Dam tailwater (south-holston-river) and the Watauga arm fed by the Wilbur Dam tailwater (watauga-river). Outflow is the Boone tailwater (boone-tailwater) down to Fort Patrick Henry Lake. Aliases: Boone Reservoir. TWRA's Boone Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources).
Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: LMB/SMB 5/day combined, 15" min; spotted bass 15/day no limit; crappie 15/day combined 10" min; striped/hybrid 2/day combined (1 striped max; 36" min striped, 15" min hybrid); (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Buffalo Creek in Grainger County, Tennessee — the TWRA-stocked trout stream near Rutledge and Tampico that runs through Buffalo Springs WMA (TWRA's 342-acre WMA with the Buffalo Springs trout hatchery on site). Explicitly a different stream from Buffalo Creek at Norris in Anderson County (USGS 03534500), as the catalog notes.
priorLeads.boundaries: TWRA regulation exceptions treat 'Buffalo Creek (and tributaries) within the WMA boundary, Grainger County' as one unit: from the mill dam upstream is closed year-round to all fishing; from the mill dam downstream is open year-round to rod-and-reel fishing. Temperature evidence cited here is from the TDEC monitoring point at the Tamipco Road bridge (36.1941,-83.5627), the same reach USGS lists as 'BUFFALO CREEK AT TAMPICO, TN' (USGS 03494530, HUC 06010104, Grainger County).

coldSourceSummary.notes: No dam on the stocked reach. TWRA's Buffalo Springs WMA page (Grainger County) places a fish hatchery on the WMA and describes Buffalo Creek itself as accessible along the WMA dirt road; the WMA sits ~1 km upstream of the Tampico gauge point, tying the stocked creek to the same watershed as the temperature record. The catchment is a ~19.6 sq mi lowland Grainger County basin (USGS 03494528 'BUFFALO CREEK NR TAMPICO' drainage area); no gorge, gradient, or canopy description found on an agency page.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover survey exists. The program structure itself documents multi-month carry-over of stocked fish: TWRA's exceptions text sets a Delayed Harvest season on Buffalo Creek (WMA boundary reach) from Oct 1 to Jan 31 with catch-and-release and artificial lures only, i.e., fall-stocked trout must survive in-stream for months to be available to the Feb 1-Sept 30 harvest season that follows.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout listing or natural-reproduction documentation found for Buffalo Creek (Grainger). The TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 treats wild trout as an East Tennessee mountain/tailwater phenomenon and lists hatchery-supported streams as warmwater habitats; Buffalo Creek appears only as a stocked stream, and all workbook stocking rows are hatchery rainbow trout. (Name collision note: TWRA's Buffalo Springs HATCHERY is on this WMA — 'Buffalo' there refers to the spring/hatchery, not a wild trout stream.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TDEC grab samples at the Tamipco Road bridge show summer water of only 15.5-19.2 C across 2010-2025 (12 Jun-Sep observations, max 19.16 C in Jul 2024), and TWRA stocks the creek weekly from February through August plus an Oct 1-Jan 31 delayed-harvest catch-and-release season — near-year-round trout presence both measured and programmatic.

catalogFields.notes:
Middle Tennessee’s signature tailwater: TWRA-stocked rainbows (stocking runs March through December) plus a celebrated winter/spring trophy brown trout program below Center Hill Dam. Generation swings are dramatic — Stonewall and at-dam gauges are your wade-window planners.

Regulations: Center Hill Dam to Cumberland River: total trout creel 5; Rainbow/Brook/Cutthroat 5/day with 14–20 in PLR, only 1 over 20 in; Brown Trout 1/day, 24-in minimum (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Caney Fork River below Center Hill Dam (Center Hill tailwater), DeKalb County
priorLeads.boundaries: Center Hill Dam down to the Cumberland River confluence; stocking and study reach is the first 26 km below the dam; Stonewall gauge reach

coldSourceSummary.notes: USACE Nashville District project; the reservoir is thermally stratified and hypolimnial release drives tailwater temperature (Devlin & Bettoli 1999, Proc. SEAFWA 53:100-109, https://seafwa.org/sites/default/files/journal-articles/DEVLIN-100-109.pdf). In June 2024 USACE reinstalled a ~120-ft-deep orifice gate establishing a 250 cfs summer/fall minimum continuous flow specifically to 'mitigat[e] the risk of elevated temperatures' and support the 'renowned cold-water trout fishery' (USACE-affiliated account). PEER report 'Last Gasp' documents historical summer/fall low-flow DO problems (https://peer.org/wp-content/uploads/attachments/05_23_8_centerhilldam.pdf). Temperature: generation-period tailwater temperatures ranged 9-19 C across 1997, the warmest at November fall turnover (Devlin & Bettoli 1999); no summer-month-attributed numeric reading is stated in that study - hence empty summerTemperature. USGS 03424860 (Caney Fork at Stonewall) is confirmed the correct tailwater-reach gauge but carries no temperature parameter (checked via https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv/?sites=03424860&parameterCd=00010&startDT=2025-07-01&endDT=2025-07-31&format=json).

holdover.detail: Devlin & Bettoli (1999): brown trout stocked in 1997 survived at 34% after 200 days post-stocking vs 7-14% for the three rainbow cohorts; i.e., stocked browns persist through summer and beyond in the tailwater.

wildPopulation.detail: No confirmed natural-reproduction anchor found in this pass. The Devlin & Bettoli (1999) study examined only stocked cohorts and reports no age-0 wild recruitment data; the fishery is managed as put-grow-take with a trophy brown program. TWRA Region IV reports may address Caney reproduction - unverified here.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Hypolimnial releases kept generation-period tailwater temperatures at 9-19 C through 1997 and 34% of stocked browns survived 200 days, with USACE now guaranteeing a 250 cfs cold-season minimum flow to protect the fishery.

waters.name: Caney Fork River (above Center Hill Lake)

catalogFields.notes:
Free-flowing upper Caney Fork from the Cumberland County headwaters down through Rock Island to the slackwater pools pooled above Center Hill Dam — Great Falls Lake (great-falls-lake) at Rock Island and the long Center Hill Lake (center-hill-lake) arms. Warmwater water: smallmouth and bream country; no trout program is documented this far above the dams and no gauge-based condition is published for this reach. The celebrated tailwater fishery begins at the dam on the caney-fork-river reach.

Regulations: Walleye run — Jan 1–Apr 30: "restricted to the use of one (1) hook having a single barb or lure containing a single hook with one barb"; max 3 rods/poles (Rock Island ramp upstream to Great Falls Dam). (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

forecastMentions.snippet: The Caney Fork River, located below the Center Hill Dam offers some of the best trout fishing in middle Tennessee. Located in Smith County near the town of Lancaster, the Caney Fork flows 26 miles before running into the Cum

priorLeads.segment: Free-flowing upper Caney Fork River above Center Hill Lake: Cumberland County headwaters down through the Great Falls Lake pool at Rock Island (Warren/White county line) to the slackwater pools pooled above Center Hill Dam. This is NOT the celebrated Center Hill Dam tailwater (cataloged separately as caney-fork-river) - the tailwater's cold-release facts do not transfer to this reach.
priorLeads.boundaries: Cumberland County headwaters downstream to the Center Hill Lake slackwater, passing through Great Falls Lake at Rock Island; the TWRA walleye-run regulation names the free-flowing span 'Rock Island State Park's boat ramp extending upstream to Great Falls Dam.'

coldSourceSummary.notes: No cold-water source documented for this reach. The USGS station at the reach's downstream end (03422500, Caney Fork near Rock Island, at Great Falls Dam) has a datum of 647.09 ft - low relative to the Cumberland Plateau headwaters upstream. TWRA manages the reach as warmwater: the Great Falls Reservoir page lists bass/crappie/catfish/walleye/musky, and the only trout program on the Caney Fork is the Center Hill TAILWATER below the dam (a different catalog reach). TWRA's weekly fishing report covers the Caney Fork as 'Center Hill Tailwater' only.

holdover.detail: No holdover is possible to document: TWRA stocks nothing into this reach (the stocking feed's only Caney Fork row is 'Center Hill TW / Caney Fork River', the tailwater below Center Hill Dam), so there is no source of trout to hold over.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented anywhere on the upper Caney Fork: the reach appears in no TWRA trout category (absent from the wild-trout list and every other trout designation on TWRA's trout regulations page), and TWRA's Great Falls Reservoir documentation describes a warmwater assemblage (largemouth/spotted/smallmouth bass, white crappie, channel and flathead catfish, walleye, musky, sunfish). A seasonal walleye run (Jan 1-Apr 30 single-hook rule, Rock Island ramp upstream to Great Falls Dam) is the documented cold-season fishery.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: USGS grab samples at Caney Fork near Rock Island (03422500) across 1964-1995 show summer water temperatures of 19-26 C (26.0 C in Jul 1971 and Aug 1985) and neither TWRA stocking nor any trout designation exists above Center Hill Dam.

priorLeads.segment: Center Hill Reservoir itself - the 18,220-acre USACE impoundment of the Caney Fork east of Smithville across DeKalb, Putnam, Warren, and White counties. Distinct from the celebrated trout tailwater below Center Hill Dam (cataloged as caney-fork-river) and from the free-flowing river above the lake (caney-fork-upper).
priorLeads.boundaries: Full pool at Center Hill Dam (Caney Fork river-mile ~26) upstream through the Caney Fork, Collins, and Calfkiller arms; county spread DeKalb/Putnam/Warren/White per TWRA.

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA states 'The United States Army Corps of Engineers is the operating authority of Center Hill Reservoir' (18,220 acres; DeKalb, Putnam, Warren, White counties). The bottom-draw release (~120-ft-deep orifice gate, reinstalled June 2024) describes the dam's deep discharge - it is what makes the TAILWATER below the dam cold, not the lake itself: the reservoir is thermally stratified (Devlin & Bettoli 1999 documented the stratification driving the hypolimnial tailwater release), and the one WQP surface reading at the near-dam reservoir station was 31.63 C in July 2012. TWRA's lake fishery page lists black bass, crappie, walleye, bluegill, catfish - no trout.

holdover.detail: No trout are stocked into the lake (TWRA's 2026 stocking feed has zero Center Hill LAKE rows - the only 'Center Hill' row is 'Center Hill TW / Caney Fork River', the tailwater below the dam), so no lake holdover is documented either way.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's reservoir page describes the fishery as black bass (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted), crappie, walleye, bluegill, catfish with detailed black-bass survey commentary and no trout mention. The lake is absent from TWRA's year-round reservoir trout stocking list (Dale Hollow, Parksville, Calderwood, Chilhowee, Fort Patrick Henry, South Holston, Tellico Upper, Watauga) verified live on TWRA's trout page this session, and absent from all trout categories on the trout regulations page.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The lake's surface water hit 31.63 C in July 2012 at the near-dam WQP station and TWRA manages it purely as a warmwater bass/crappie fishery with no trout stocking; whether trout could survive year-round in its cold hypolimnion is untested because TWRA has never put a trout program on the lake.

TVA reservoir on the Holston River northeast of Knoxville across Grainger, Hamblen, Hawkins, and Jefferson counties, impounded by Cherokee Dam (USGS 03493510 tailwater gauge, 36.16620/-83.49934). Receives the Holston River main stem (holston-river); its dam releases the Holston Cherokee tailwater that runs to Fort Loudoun Lake. TWRA maps the pool at 27,029 ac; TVA at 30,300 ac at full pool. TWRA's Cherokee Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources). Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: Largemouth/Smallmouth 5/day combined, Largemouth 15-in min; Smallmouth Jun 1–Oct 15 = 1/day 18-in min, Oct 16–May 31 = 5/day 15-in min; Spotted/Alabama 15/day no limit; Crappie 15/day 10-in; Striper/hybrid 2/day 15-in; Walleye/Sauger/Saugeye 10/day 15-in; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Cherokee Lake (Cherokee Reservoir), the TVA impoundment of the Holston River across Grainger, Hamblen, Hawkins, and Jefferson counties northeast of Knoxville, impounded at its southwest end by Cherokee Dam. TWRA's fishery description covers the 30,300-surface-acre pool itself.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire reservoir pool (TWRA: 30,300 ac, 393 mi shoreline; TVA owns up to the 1,075-ft contour). Excludes the Holston River Cherokee tailwater below Cherokee Dam, which is stocked by TWRA and is a separate catalog entry.

damTailwater.dam: Cherokee Dam (TVA) impounds the lake; the dam's cold deep releases form the downstream Holston River Cherokee tailwater, which is a different catalog entry and does not cold-water this pool

coldSourceSummary.notes: Full-pool contour 1,075 ft per TWRA's Cherokee Reservoir page ('TVA owns up to the 1,075-ft...'). TWRA: 'The reservoir thermally stratifies in the summer when warm oxygenated surface water cannot mix with the cold [deeper water]... During most summers and in many locations, oxygen levels below 30 ft. can become too low to support most fish species.' On-lake TDEC profile station TDECWPC-HOLST093.5HSS/HOLST093.5HSB 'CHEROKEE LAKE NEAR JOHNSON HOLLOW' (HUC 06010104) recorded 27.0 C surface / 24.4 C bottom on 2000-08-09. USGS identity note: identity endpoint was down this week; stations verified via WQP Station search CSV (e.g. USGS-03493510 'HOLSTON RIVER AT CHEROKEE DAM(TW), TN', HUC 06010104).

holdover.detail: Not applicable as a trout question - no trout fishery is documented for the reservoir. TWRA notes even the coldwater-striped-bass program is marginal here: stripers 'must be maintained by stocking' and 'do not normally grow big in Cherokee Reservoir, due to low summer dissolved [oxygen]'.

wildPopulation.detail: No trout population of any kind documented. TWRA's Cherokee Reservoir 'What you can catch' page lists Largemouth, Smallmouth, Striped, Cherokee (striper x white hybrid) bass, Crappie, Walleye, Saugeye, Paddlefish, White Bass, Bluegill, Catfish - no trout species appear anywhere in the fishery text (the only 'trout' strings on the page are navigation-menu items).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA documents a warmwater fishery with no trout; the lake thermally stratifies each summer with 27 C surface water (TDEC on-lake profile, Aug 2000) and oxygen below 30 ft too low for most fish in most summers, and Cherokee is absent from TWRA's year-round reservoir trout stocking list while eight other reservoirs are on it.

priorLeads.segment: Chestuee Creek, a Hiwassee River tributary draining McMinn County (HUC 06020002 Hiwassee) toward the Hiwassee arm of Chickamauga Lake. Two USGS stations document the stream: 03565120 'CHESTUEE CREEK AT ZION HILL, TN' (upper, 37.8 sq mi, gage datum 778 ft) and 03565250 'CHESTUEE CREEK AT DENTVILLE TENN (TVA)' (lower, 114 sq mi, gage datum 723 ft). No trout program of any kind exists on the creek.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog gives no reach limits; record covers the McMinn County main stem from the Zion Hill area downstream past Dentville to the Hiwassee/Chickamauga Lake confluence.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Gage datum 723 ft (NGVD29) at lower station 03565250 (TVA co-op era); upper station 03565120 sits at 778 ft - a low-to-mid elevation Valley-and-Ridge tributary, not a cold mountain stream. The 03565120/03565250 identity, county (McMinn, FIPS 107), drainage areas, and datums were verified on the USGS waterservices site endpoint.

holdover.detail: Not applicable - no trout have ever been stocked: TWRA's stocking workbook contains zero 'Chestuee' rows, the creek has no entry on TWRA's trout regulations page (delayed harvest, wild trout, or special regulation lists), and it is never mentioned in the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documentation of any kind found. The Trout Management Plan places wild trout in East Tennessee mountain streams; Chestuee Creek is a lowland Valley-and-Ridge agricultural tributary (TDEC has listed it for siltation/biological-integrity impairment in past 303(d) cycles per search leads, not re-verified to a primary document here).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Control-style warmwater record: zero TWRA stocking rows, no trout regulation or Trout Management Plan mention, no wild-trout documentation, and no water temperature record at all for this ~723-ft McMinn County Hiwassee tributary.

priorLeads.segment: Chickamauga Lake - the mainstem Tennessee River reservoir impounded by TVA's Chickamauga Dam, spanning Hamilton, Bradley, Meigs, and Rhea counties from Watts Bar Dam downstream to Chickamauga Dam (HUC 06020001), receiving the Hiwassee River. TWRA maps the pool at 33,973 ac. The catalog's species list (largemouth/smallmouth/spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass) is a warmwater fishery; no trout fishery exists on the reservoir.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire reservoir: Watts Bar Dam tailwater to Chickamauga Dam. Tailwater identity: USGS 03566510 'TENNESSEE RIVER AT CHICKAMAUGA DAM (TW)' (35.10313/-85.22968, 20,790 sq mi drainage, gage datum 626.5 ft). Note: the stocked 'N. Chickamauga Creek' in TWRA's schedule is a separate tributary creek, not the reservoir.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Elevation is TVA's typical summer operating range (681.5-682.5 ft) for the reservoir; the 03566510 tailwater gage datum is 626.5 ft. Chickamauga Dam is a mainstem hydroelectric facility. No cold deep-draw release regime is documented - a mainstream storage impoundment, unlike TVA's deep-storage tributary dams. Historic tailwater grabs at 03566510 (below the dam) reached 27.5 C in August 1977, confirming warm releases.

holdover.detail: Not applicable - no trout are stocked: TWRA's stocking workbook contains zero rows for Chickamauga Lake (the only 'Chickamauga' rows are for North Chickamauga Creek, a distinct tributary stream). TWRA's Chickamauga Reservoir page states the only species TWRA stocks there are striped bass, walleye, and Florida largemouth bass.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA's own Chickamauga Reservoir page lists the fishery as warmwater species (largemouth/spotted/smallmouth bass, crappie, bluegill, redear, sauger/walleye, catfish, white/yellow bass, striped/hybrid bass, paddlefish) with no trout mention of any kind; and the TWRA Trout Management Plan's list of the nine Tennessee reservoirs that 'currently support trout fisheries' (Dale Hollow, Parksville, South Holston, Wilbur, Watauga, Fort Patrick Henry, Calderwood, Chilhowee, Tellico) does not include Chickamauga.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A mainstem warmwater reservoir whose tailwater grabs hit 27.5 C in August: TWRA stocks no trout in it, TWRA's reservoir fishery page names no trout at all, and the Trout Management Plan's nine-reservoir trout list excludes it.

priorLeads.segment: Citico Creek main stem, Monroe County, in the Cherokee National Forest, flowing north to Tellico Lake (Little Tennessee HUC 06010204). The catalog covers both the stocked main stem and the wild-trout headwater forks. TWRA's Tellico-Citico Permit Area regulates the creek from its confluence with Little Citico Creek upstream to the confluence of the North and South Forks; the North/South Fork headwaters (incl. Falls Branch, a South Fork tributary) hold the documented wild brook trout.
priorLeads.boundaries: Permitted reach: Little Citico Creek confluence upstream to the North/South Fork junction (TWRA trout regulations page). Stocked reach is the main stem; wild trout are documented in the forks above.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Elevation figure applies to the headwaters, not the main stem: the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 places Goat Falls on North Fork Citico Creek 'at ~3,200' (brook trout habitat discussion) - https://www.tn.gov/content/dam/tn/twra/documents/fishing/Tennessee-Trout-Management-Plan-2017-2027.pdf . The plan also describes the watershed as steep, remote, rain-flashy Cherokee NF terrain. No dam on the creek; cold source is forested mountain headwater elevation.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover study found. The main stem receives 22 consecutive weekly TWRA seasonal stockings (weeks of 2/22 through 7/19 in the 2026 schedule) and the permit area remains open to daily fishing Aug 16 - end of February without a permit, which implies fish availability into fall/winter, but no creel or tag-return evidence of holdover was located.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 documents that until recently two streams in the Citico Creek watershed supported brook trout - upper North Fork Citico Creek and Falls Branch (South Fork Citico tributary); a 2013 distribution survey found only the Falls Branch population remains (naturalized, hatchery origin per 1990s genetics), with North Fork Citico extirpated above Goat Falls. USFS Cherokee NF states 'Wild trout, rainbow, brown and native brookies are present in most of the mountain streams above 1000 feet' (general CNF statement, not Citico-specific). The stocked main stem itself is not a wild trout water and is NOT on TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A naturalized brook trout population persisted in the watershed (Falls Branch, 2013 TWRA survey) - documented year-round survival in the headwaters - while the stocked main stem showed ~23 C grab temperatures in June 2014 near its mouth, consistent with its put-grow-take role rather than fail.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: NPS surveys at five Clear Creek transects recorded zero salmonids and the Lilly Bridge gauge reached 29.0 C on 2026-07-03 (NRCA continuous record topped 30 C in summer 2016).

coldSourceSummary.notes: TVA describes constant deep releases from Norris keeping the tailwater near 50 F year-round (TVA 'Big Ones Below Norris'). Downstream the reach is impounded by Melton Hill Lake, which buffers/warms the lower river toward Kingston; trout-grade cold water ends roughly 13 miles below the dam (guide consensus, not agency-quantified). TWRA weekly reports have cited ~48 F water 'coming out of the dam' in summer (https://www.tn.gov/twra/fishing/weekly-fishing-report.html).

holdover.detail: Bettinger & Bettoli (2004, North American Journal of Fisheries Management 24; DOI 10.1577/M03-144.1) radiotracked 15 trophy brown trout below Norris Dam for a full year; fish held in the tailwater year-round with limited movement (<2 km) in winter, spring and summer, and 2-4 lb fish are routine in the fishery.

wildPopulation.detail: Inferred but not nailed to a citable agency age-0 survey in this pass: Bettinger & Bettoli (2004) report fall movements >5 km 'presumably to spawn', and AFS Southern Division Trout Committee minutes (2002) quote TWRA's Jim Habera that sampling indicated natural rainbow reproduction from a Tennessee tailwater — but neither document confirms in-tailwater age-0 recruitment for the Clinch specifically. TWRA Region IV trout reports (Habera) are the likely authority; not verified in this pass.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TVA-documented deep-release temperatures near 50 F year-round below Norris Dam, with radio-telemetry showing trophy browns resident in the tailwater through all seasons.

priorLeads.segment: The Collins River, a 67-mile Cumberland Plateau river flowing from Grundy County (Savage Gulf gorge headwaters) to its confluence with the Caney Fork above Great Falls Dam. Cataloged with USGS gauge 03421000 (Collins River near McMinnville, mid-basin, below the Barren Fork confluence); TWRA's stocked reach is the lower/mid river.
priorLeads.boundaries: Grundy and Warren counties; HUC 05130107 (Collins subbasin). The 6.4-mile Scenic River segment lies in the Savage Gulf gorge in the upper reach; temperature evidence below is from the near-McMinnville gauge on the lower-mid river.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No cold-water source documented for the stocked reach. TDEC documents the UPPER scenic segment (Savage Gulf gorge) as a losing stream that 'flows predominantly underground... except during periods of heavy rainfall' - the gorge headwaters are intermittently dewatered by karst sinks, not a reliable cold source. TDEC: beyond the scenic stretch the Collins is 'one of few rivers in Tennessee with a good population of muskie,' a warmwater indicator for the main river.

holdover.detail: No agency documentation of holdover either way. TWRA stocks the Collins only in spring/early summer (three seasonal 2026 weeks: 3/1, 3/22, 5/10, Rainbow Trout); no summer or winter stocking rows and no creel or sampling evidence of between-stocking survival were found.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented: the Collins appears in no TWRA trout-regulation category (absent from the wild-trout list and every special-regulation section of TWRA's trout regulations page, checked live this session), and the fisheries TWRA/TDEC document for the river are musky and black bass.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: USGS 03421000 at McMinnville recorded summer water temperatures up to 29.5 C (Aug 1986; 27.5-29 C in four other summers of 1964-2005) while TWRA stocks the Collins only in spring/early summer - seasonal put-and-take rainbow with no documented between-stocking survival.

priorLeads.segment: Conasauga River (GNIS 00327507), Coosa-basin drainage — restricted to the TENNESSEE reaches the catalog entry covers. TDEC designates the Tennessee reach as a State Scenic River: 'The entire segment of the river in Polk County, upstream from the Highway 411 bridge', Class I Natural River Area, designated April 23, 1969, ~10.1 miles, one of only two Tennessee Scenic Rivers in the Cherokee National Forest. The river crosses the TN/GA line more than once near Tennga; the famous rare-species research (Conasauga logperch, amber darter, listed mussels) and Georgia's 2015 Outstanding National Resource Water designation apply to the GEORGIA reaches (Cohutta Wilderness headwaters, Jacks River) and are NOT attributed to the Tennessee reach here.
priorLeads.boundaries: Polk County segments of the river upstream of the US-411 bridge (take-out 35.00888, -84.73389, at the state line near Tennga) per the TDEC Scenic Rivers designation; the USGS gauge 02384000 'CONASAUGA RIVER AT US 411, NEAR TENNGA' (35.0095, -84.7338, 108 sq mi — listed under Polk County TN, operated by the USGS Georgia center) sits at the downstream boundary of this reach.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Freestone river draining the Cohutta Mountains through the Cherokee National Forest; the Tennessee scenic segment is a narrow valley run with Class II-III rapids per TDEC's paddling description. No dam, no spring-influence documentation for the TN reach. Gauge altitude at the US-411 boundary is ~756 ft (USGS 02384000), so the TN reach is low-elevation; no agency statement on TN-reach summer cold-water refuge was located.

holdover.detail: No trout presence of any kind documented for the Tennessee reach — no stocking program rows, no trout designation, no creel or angler documentation located — so holdover cannot be assessed.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented in the Tennessee reach. TDEC's Scenic River page describes a rich native fish community — 'more than 90 fish species and 25 mussel species' with federal and state-listed aquatic species — and names no trout. The celebrated rare-fish work and any trout headwater fishery (Cohutta Wilderness, Jacks River, GA's 2015 ONRW designation) are on the Georgia reaches and do not transfer to the TN reach. TWRA's stocking workbook contains zero Conasauga rows, and the river is absent from TWRA's wild-trout/special-regulation lists.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The only summer data for the Tennessee reach — USGS grabs at the US-411 state-line crossing bounding it — read 20.0-24.0 degC (1957-1996), marginal for trout, and no source documents any trout presence, stocking, or fishery on the TN reach itself.

priorLeads.segment: Cosby Creek, Cocke County — Great Smoky Mountains National Park stream draining the Cosby area (GNIS 01327978, HUC 06010106). Catalog note describes wild rainbows and brook trout upstream with park-wide NPS regulations.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog covers the creek generically; no sub-reach boundaries documented. TWRA 2026 stocking schedule lists 'Cosby Creek' (Cocke County) seasonally without specifying stocked access points relative to the park boundary.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No cold-source documentation found specific to Cosby Creek. Park context only: NPS states the park safeguards 'one of the last remaining wild trout habitats in the eastern United States' across ~2,900 stream miles (https://www.nps.gov/grsm/planyourvisit/fishing.htm).

holdover.detail: No holdover-specific evidence sought/found. Holdover is largely moot here because NPS has not stocked the park since 1975 — trout present are resident wild fish, not seasonal stockers.

wildPopulation.detail: NPS: stocking of non-native trout in GSMNP ended in 1975 as 'inconsistent with NPS policies' (restoration stocking only for native non-game species); monitoring shows healthy wild trout densities of 2,000-4,000 fish/mile park-wide. Stream-specific: NPS brook trout research names Cosby Creek directly ('a brook trout caught at Cosby Creek is still classified the same species of fish as a brook trout caught at Lynn Camp Prong'), and the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 names Cosby Creek as a potential donor stream for native brook trout restoration. CONFLICT to flag: the TWRA 2026 stocking schedule (packages/content/data/twra-stocking-schedule.json, sourced from tn.gov) lists 'Cosby Creek', Cocke County, seasonal Rainbow Trout weeks 3/1-6/21/2026 — while NPS says the park does not stock. The stocked location relative to the park boundary is not documented in sources consulted; both facts stand as recorded.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: NPS has managed the park's streams as unstocked wild trout water since 1975 and agency sources (NPS and TWRA) document brook trout in Cosby Creek itself — a self-sustaining resident population by definition.

priorLeads.segment: Cumberland River main stem, Nashville-to-Lake Barkley reach across Davidson to Stewart counties (catalog) — the pool-and-navigation-river continuum below Old Hickory Dam through Nashville (USGS gage 03431500, drainage 12,856 sq mi) and on to the Kentucky line. This is the Tennessee main stem; the South Fork Cumberland is a separate water, and the trout-bearing Cumberland tailwater is in Kentucky, not Tennessee.
priorLeads.boundaries: Per catalog: Nashville to Lake Burkley (Lake Barkley), Davidson through Stewart counties, TN; impounded in pools behind USACE navigation/flood dams (Old Hickory Dam at river mile 216.2 forms the upstream pool boundary).

damTailwater.dam: Old Hickory Dam (pool boundary at Nashville reach)

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA states 'The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) owns and operates Old Hickory Reservoir', a 22,500-acre impoundment on the Cumberland River (dam completed 1954). No source documents a cold-release trout regime on the Tennessee main stem; TWRA's Region 2 tailwater trout list does not include any Cumberland main-stem reach. KDFWR documents that the Cumberland trout tailwater (below Wolf Creek Dam, KY) runs 'from Wolf Creek Dam downstream to the Tennessee state line' — i.e., the managed trout water ends at the Tennessee line and does not include this TN main-stem segment.

holdover.detail: No trout holdover or trout fishery of any kind is documented on this main-stem segment: TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule lists no Cumberland main-stem stocking location (the only 'Cumberland' entries are Cumberland County park/tributary waters in Region 3), TWRA's Region 2 tailwater list has no Cumberland main-stem entry, and the workbook has no main-stem trout rows. Winter rainbow stockings at 'Shelby Bottoms' and 'Cedar Hill Park Pond' (Davidson Co.) are park-pond/adjacent program sites, not a documented open-main-stem trout fishery.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented for the Tennessee main stem. TWRA's reservoir/species documentation for this reach is entirely warmwater (black bass, crappie, sauger, striped/hybrid bass, walleye, catfish), and the managed Cumberland trout fishery documented by Kentucky lies above the Tennessee state line in the Lake Cumberland tailwater.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Warm USACE navigation/reservoir main stem: TWRA documents no trout program anywhere on the TN main stem, KDFWR places the managed Cumberland trout tailwater entirely above the Tennessee state line, and the only summer grab sample on record (gage 03431500) is 21.1 C in late September 1995.

priorLeads.segment: Daddy's Creek (Cumberland County), gorge water in the Obed system, running its full named length to the Obed confluence near Hebbertsburg; lower reach inside Obed Wild & Scenic River.
priorLeads.boundaries: Headwaters in Cumberland County (USGS 03539600 near Hebbertsburg at 35.9977, -84.8225) downstream to the confluence with the Obed River; TDEC scenic-river designation covers Daddy's Creek from the Morgan County line to its Obed confluence.

coldSourceSummary.notes: No dam tailwater: TDEC's Obed scenic-river designation includes Daddy's Creek from the Morgan County line to its Obed confluence as part of the free-flowing Wild & Scenic system. Elevation is the USGS 03539600 gauge near Hebbertsburg (1444.69 ft). NRCA: Daddy's Creek 1982-1998 temperatures ranged 0.3-28.4 C with the highest in July and September (mean 14.1 C).

holdover.detail: No trout fishery documented on this water (see wildPopulation), so holdover evidence was not sought or found.

wildPopulation.detail: NPS fish-assemblage inventories document zero trout: Russ (2006) sampled two Daddy's Creek locations inside Obed WSR (19 species, whitetail/telescope shiners, rock bass, smallmouth) and Scott (2010b) found 13 species; the park's certified 55-species fish list (Appendix G) contains no Salmonidae, and a text search of the full NRCA report returns zero 'trout' hits. Daddy's Creek is also absent from TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule and wild-trout-stream list.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: NPS surveys at two Daddy's Creek park locations recorded zero salmonids and the Hebbertsburg gauge reached 30.0 C on 2026-07-02.

priorLeads.segment: Entire Dale Hollow Reservoir (USACE Obey River impoundment; 25,519 ac total per KDFWR, with 6,614 ac in Kentucky), at the Kentucky line in Clay, Pickett, Overton (and Fentress) counties, TN and Clinton/Cumberland counties, KY. coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA: 'The operating authority is the U.S. Corps of Engineers' (dam completed 1943 on the Obey River). USACE Nashville District water-control documentation lists normal pool 651.0 ft msl (verified only via search snippet of the USACE Dale Hollow water control manual; full URL not captured, so elevation left null). Adjacent USFWS Dale Hollow NFH exists to mitigate federal-dam impacts by 'stocking rainbow, brown, lake, and brook trout in waters impacted by federal dams' — i.e., primarily the cold tailwaters below the dam, not the lake.

holdover.detail: TWRA's reservoir page documents persistence across seasons: 'Rainbow trout are typically stocked annually into Dale Hollow Reservoir during the wintertime,' and anglers 'begin trolling for trout in deeper water near the dam in May,' June is best (downriggers, spoons in 30-50 ft), with trout also caught 'in the summer months at night' — winter-stocked trout documented in the creel guidance through early summer. Composition conflict (flagged by catalog owner): the live TWRA page describes wintertime rainbow stocking, while the TWRA stocking workbook row reads 'Dale Hollow Reservoir / Reservoir / April / Brown Trout', and the TWRA program list reads 'Region II, Dale Hollow, - Rainbow'.

wildPopulation.detail: No documentation found of natural trout reproduction in the reservoir; fisheries rely on annual stocking (TWRA page; USFWS hatchery program).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA documents winter stocking of rainbow trout into the reservoir AND a summer deep-water fishery for them (trolling near the dam from May, best in June, summer night fishing), and lists Dale Hollow among reservoirs stocked 'to provide year-round trout fishing opportunities' — multi-season survival of stocked trout is documented by the managing agency itself.

priorLeads.segment: Doe Creek (GNIS 01328063), a tributary of Roan Creek in Johnson County, TN (HUC 06010103 Watauga) that joins Roan Creek near Doeville. This is NOT the Doe River of Carter County (a separate catalog entry evidenced in batch 3). Identity verified via WQP station metadata: TDEC stations named 'Doe Creek' with CountyCode 091 (Johnson) and HUCEightDigitCode 06010103, spanning river-mile ~1.2 (36.3831,-81.9561) to river-mile ~7.6 (36.4344,-81.9139). USGS's own monitoring-location identity service was persistently 503 this week, so station name/county/HUC columns in the WQP CSV were used.
priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog gives no reach limits and TWRA stocks it countywide as 'Doe Creek'. Record covers the main stem from the upper TDEC station (RM 7.6 near Little Doe) to the mouth at Roan Creek near Doeville; eRegulations' walleye-run reach is 'Old Cabin Private Road downstream to Roan Creek'.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Free-flowing mountain tributary in the Watauga HUC (06010103); TDEC's Jan 2002 grab at RM 7.6 read 8.16 C and at RM 1.2 read 4.34 C, consistent with a cold upland stream. Corroborating agency context (not trout-specific): the creek's lower reach is one of the few Region 4 waters TWRA/eRegulations protect with a Jan 1-Apr 30 one-hook walleye-run restriction ('Doe Creek (Old Cabin Private Road downstream to Roan Creek)'), a restriction TWRA applies to cold spawning-run tributaries of Watauga Lake country. No gorge/canopy citation found.

holdover.detail: No holdover-specific creel or angler-verified documentation found for Doe Creek. A documented wild trout population (below) necessarily implies multi-season in-stream survival, but over-summer survival of stocked fish specifically is not separately documented.

wildPopulation.detail: TWRA Fisheries Report 18-01 (Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2017): 'Some stocked steams (e.g., Beaverdam Creek, Doe Creek, Laurel Fork, and Doe River) do support excellent wild trout populations as well.' In that report's Johnson County context 'Doe Creek' is this Roan Creek tributary (the batch-3 Doe River record flagged the same sentence and explicitly identified its 'Doe Creek' as the Johnson County water). The report further characterizes the creek as one of the region's productive wild trout streams alongside its seasonal hatchery-supported fishery. Species composition of the wild component is not stated in the cited sentence. Note: the creek is NOT on TWRA's current Wild Trout Streams special-regulation list (that list's only Johnson County entry is Beaverdam Creek), so the wild fishery runs under statewide trout rules.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA's own Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2017 documents an excellent wild trout population in this exact creek - wild reproduction requires year-round in-stream survival - and TDEC grab samples 2001-2026 show summer peaks of only 14.9-18.2 C.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA's Region IV Trout Fisheries Report 2017 names Doe River among stocked streams that 'support excellent wild trout populations' (Appendix A: 14 quantitative samples 1995-2015, RBT/BKT/BNT) - a self-sustaining population is by definition year-round; note the lowermost Elizabethton reach is the warm part (historical July-August gauge samples there reached 24-24.5 C).

catalogFields.notes:
TVA reservoir on the French Broad River east of Knoxville across Cocke, Jefferson, Sevier, and Hamblen counties, impounded by Douglas Dam (USGS 03468510 tailwater gauge, 35.96120/-83.53878). Receives the French Broad River and the Pigeon River; discharges through the dam into the French Broad tailwater toward the Holston/French Broad confluence. TWRA maps the reservoir at 28,738 ac. Aliases: Douglas Reservoir. TWRA's Douglas Reservoir page lists the fishery as largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, spotted bass, crappie, bluegill, catfish, striped bass (see officialSources). Striped bass is a regulatory or hybrid-evidence tag here; reservoir temperature/oxygen refuge context is not a scored input.

Regulations: black bass 5/day; Oct 1–May 31 no length limit; Jun 1–Sep 30 only one LMB/SMB >16 in/day; crappie 15/day, 10-in min; catfish 1/day >34 in; white/striped/hybrid 15/day; walleye+sauger 5/day combined, walleye 15-in min; muskellunge 1/day 36-in min; (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.segment: Douglas Lake (TVA Douglas Reservoir) — the TVA impoundment of the French Broad River east of Knoxville across Cocke, Jefferson, Sevier and Hamblen counties, impounded by Douglas Dam (USGS 03468510 tailwater gauge at the dam, Sevier County). Receives the French Broad River and the Pigeon River; discharges through the dam into the French Broad tailwater. Sibling of the cataloged french-broad-river tailwater, which batch 1 documented as a warmwater control — this record addresses the LAKE itself with lake-specific evidence.
priorLeads.boundaries: Entire reservoir; TWRA full-pool harvest-restriction boundary extends up the Nolichucky to ENKA Dam, up the Pigeon to the Hwy 321 bridge at Newport, and up the French Broad to the Hwy 321 bridge. 30,600 acres, 555 miles of shoreline (TWRA); summer pool 1,000 ft with winter drawdown to ~940 ft.

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA describes Douglas as 'a fertile, Tennessee Valley Authority reservoir' whose pool 'can fluctuate 60 feet from the summer elevation of 1000 feet above sea level to the winter elevation of 940 feet', with 'thermal stratification... common during the summer months' and 'low dissolved oxygen concentrations... common during the summer' — a warm, fertile tributary impoundment, not a cold hypolimnetic-release body. No TVA release-depth specification is machine-verifiable (tva.com blocks automated fetch). Angling context per TWRA: in summer, fish hold below the thermocline and fishing is 'at depths of less than 10 feet (above the thermocline)'.

holdover.detail: No trout are stocked in the reservoir — the owner-supplied 2026 TWRA schedule (live feed re-verified 2026-09-18) contains zero 'Douglas' trout rows — and TWRA's reservoir page documents supplemental stocking only for sauger/walleye ('hatchery-reared fish are stocked if numbers become low'). There is no stocked-trout population to hold over; the same finding was made for the tailwater reach in the batch 1 french-broad-river control record.

wildPopulation.detail: No trout in TWRA's reservoir species account (largemouth bass 'one of the best largemouth bass fisheries in east Tennessee', 'best crappie reservoir in East Tennessee', bluegill, catfish, smallmouth, spotted bass, sauger/walleye, white bass); the reservoir has no entry on TWRA's wild trout or delayed-harvest lists.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Lake-specific evidence matches the tailwater control: zero TWRA trout stocking rows, a TWRA species account with no trout, and USGS grab samples at the dam (03468510) showing release water climbing to 26.5-27.0 C by August-September (1975-1980) in a reservoir TWRA documents as summer-stratified with low dissolved oxygen.

priorLeads.segment: Duck River mainstem from Shelbyville (Bedford County) downstream to Columbia (Maury County), through Bedford, Marshall and Maury counties. The duck-river-tailwater catalog entry (dam to Three Forks Bridge area) is upstream and is a separate water.

coldSourceSummary.notes: Reach-specific USGS/TDEC grab record documents classic warmwater temps: summer highs of 25-28 deg C at Shelbyville and 28-32 deg C at Columbia.

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation exists for this reach and none is expected: TWRA stocks no trout anywhere on this reach (workbook has zero rows from Shelbyville to Columbia), and TWRA's own biologist text - written for the cooler tailwater immediately upstream - says river water temperatures 'usually warm above the 70 F mark' outside the Nov-Jun stocking season, 'exceeding the upper limit for trout survival'.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout presence documented in this reach; TWRA documents smallmouth/spotted bass, rock bass and catfish as the fishery. Winter put-and-take programs in the same counties (Big Rock Greenway, Marshall Co.; McCutcheon Creek, Maury Co.) are separate tributary/greenway waters, not the Duck mainstem.

troutSpecies.note: TWRA's page lists Rainbow Trout among the Duck River's fisheries, but every documented trout element on the page (Nov-Jun rainbow stocking dam-to-Three-Forks-Bridge, 7-trout creel) belongs to the tailwater reach ABOVE Shelbyville - a different catalog entry. No trout stocking or trout fishery is documented within Shelbyville-to-Columbia.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Reach-specific USGS/TDEC grab records show 25-28 deg C summer water at Shelbyville and 28-32 deg C at Columbia, and TWRA stocks no trout here while stating even the cooler tailwater above Shelbyville exceeds the trout-survival limit outside the Nov-Jun stocking window.

coldSourceSummary.notes: TVA includes the Normandy tailwater in its cold-water trout program, but the TWRA-commissioned creel study found dam discharges EXCEED the 22 C downstream temperature target every summer, and September-October 2000 dam-area temperatures were 'the highest recorded in any Tennessee tailwater managed for trout' (Bettoli 2001, TWRA Fisheries Report 01-43, https://duckriveragency.org/_assets_/plugins/Annotated%20Bibliography/NormandyTW2000CreelSurvey.pdf).

holdover.detail: TWRA electrofishing in 1998 found FEW rainbow trout hold over from one season to the next, attributed to elevated late-summer/fall water temperatures (Bettoli 2001, TWRA Fisheries Report 01-43). The same report states stocking in late summer when temperatures routinely exceed 25 C 'is clearly a waste of resources'. NOTE (2026-09-17 owner policy): absence of holdover does NOT rule out year-round status - a continuously stocked reach qualifies on its own. This fact is one facet, not the verdict.

wildPopulation.detail: No natural-reproduction data found for this tailwater in the creel report or elsewhere in this pass; unknown.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Evidence points both ways and the decisive fact is unresolved: TWRA's 2000 study found lethal summer temperatures below the dam, yet the owner confirms year-round stocking (which under the 2026-09-17 owner policy would itself define a year-round trout fishery) while the 2026-09-17 workbook shows winter-months-only stocking - the current stocking regime sits in the owner box.

holdover.detail: No holdover evidence for this reach. The only Lincoln County entry in the TWRA 2026 stocking schedule is 'Stone Bridge Park' (Winter, week of 2/5/2026, Rainbow Trout) — and Stone Bridge Park Pond is a town park pond at Norris Creek and the Elk River behind Walgreens in Fayetteville (TWRA event page), i.e., a winter community-pond stocking, not mainstem stocking of the Prospect-to-state-line reach. Catalog note claims 'winter stocking in the lower county reaches'; the 2026 workbook supports only the Fayetteville pond event, and the tailwater row itself is stocked March-December (no Jan/Feb).

wildPopulation.detail: No trout records found for the Prospect-to-state-line reach. Nearest mainstem gauge (03582000, Elk River above Fayetteville — upstream of the reach) recorded a July 2025 mean of 24.95 C (max 27.8 C), June mean 21.6 C, August mean 23.5 C — warmwater mainstem conditions. Supporting (semi-authoritative tourism, not sole evidence): Tennessee River Valley Geotourism describes the tailwater transitioning into smallmouth water downstream toward Fayetteville and Prospect. overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: A shallow navigable mainstem Tennessee River pool (807-813 ft, six-foot drawdown) with documented summer temperatures of 20.6-27.0 C in the reservoir (TDEC 2011-2026) and 19-27 C in its own dam tailwater (USGS 03499510, 1975-1979), zero trout stocking rows, and no trout content in TWRA's fishery profile — excluded from the STMP's nine cold-water trout reservoirs.

priorLeads.segment: Gap Creek in Claiborne County, Tennessee — the stocked trout creek that rises at Cumberland Gap and runs southeast through Cumberland Gap National Historical Park and the town of Cumberland Gap down the Powell Valley toward the Powell River near Arthur. priorLeads.boundaries: Full named length per catalog ('runs its full named length down toward the upper Clinch' drainage). Cool summer grab samples at five separate park stations (below) are consistent with a shaded, upland-gradient creek, but no agency page states a spring or groundwater source.

holdover.detail: No site-specific holdover documentation found. TWRA's documented program is three spring Seasonal stockings (Feb 15, Mar 15, Apr 12, 2026; Rainbow Trout) with no delayed-harvest season, so there is no program mechanism that requires or documents carry-over.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout record found for Gap Creek (Claiborne). coldSourceSummary.notes: No dam; no spring-fed characterization on record. Cool-water signal is observational, not structural: TDEC monitoring shows June-September surface water of 17.5-21.7 C at both the upper and lower stations (2020-2025), and the TWRA Trout Management Plan documents reproducing native Brook Trout in the stream's tributaries — a habitat that stays trout-viable through summer.

wildPopulation.detail: Reach caveat: the documented wild trout are in the TRIBUTARIES, not necessarily the stocked main reach. TWRA's Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 twice identifies 'Gulf Fork of Big Creek tributaries (Middle Prong Gulf Creek or Brown Gap Creek)' as a donor source of native Brook Trout for planned restoration projects (Table 1: 'Use fish from Gulf Fork tribs'; Little Paint Creek rationale), which documents a self-sustaining native Brook Trout population in this stream system's headwater tributaries.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery of any kind is documented on the Hatchie. The river is absent from TWRA's live trout stocking list (checked 2026-09-18) and from the TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 (zero mentions of 'Hatchie'); that plan states hatchery-supported waters 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round'. Absence of a program is documented; absence of individual stocked fish was not surveyed.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TDEC's scenic-river page describes >100 native fish species including 11 catfish species with no trout; TWRA's Trout Management Plan contains no Hatchie reference.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Free-flowing warmwater swamp river: USGS grab samples at the Bolivar gage (07029500, 88 summer samples 1976-2005) peaked at 31.0 C in July 1986 and still hit 28.5 C in August 2005, and TWRA stocks no trout anywhere on the river.

The Southeast’s big tailwater: TWRA-managed delayed-harvest-free trophy water with wild-strength rainbow, brown and some brook trout, and famous summer evening hatches (White Fly, Yellow Sally). A winter catch-and-release season (Oct 1–Feb 28) keeps the river fishable all year. Two- and four-turbine releases swing flow hard — the Reliance gauge is the call. The tailwater runs from the Appalachia Dam release water at the NC line through Reliance to the Chickamauga Lake head.

Regulations: Appalachia Powerhouse downstream to L&N Railroad Bridge: Mar 1–Sep 30 — 7-trout creel, only 2 may be brown trout; Catch-and-Release season Oct 1–Feb 28 (artificial lures only, no harvest/possession) (retrieved 2026-09-14; verify current rules with TWRA before you go).

priorLeads.boundaries: Catalog entry says 'Appalachia Dam release water at the NC line through Reliance to the Chickamauga Lake head'; research shows the cold trout water begins at Apalachia POWERHOUSE - a pipeline/tunnel carries release water ~8.3 miles downstream from the dam, so the first ~10 miles of riverbed below the dam are bypassed and are not the trout water (TVA; TU Hiwassee chapter). coldSourceSummary.notes: TVA describes Apalachia Reservoir as 'a small, deep, cool-water reservoir' whose water is carried ~8.3 miles by pipeline/tunnel to the powerhouse - i.e. deep (cold) source water for the trout reach. USGS 03556590 (Hiwassee River above Reliance, ~759 ft elevation) is the correct trout-reach gauge; catalog's other gauge 03566000 is Hiwassee River AT CHARLESTON, far downstream near the Chickamauga head - wrong reach for trout temperatures (verified via USGS site catalog).

holdover.detail: No agency survival figure found in this pass. The delayed-harvest program (stocked Feb/Oct/Nov per TWRA workbook, catch-and-release Oct 1-Feb 28) structurally requires multi-month carry-over of stocked fish from fall to spring, but no published Hiwassee-specific holdover estimate was located.

wildPopulation.detail: TVA's tailwater trout page says cold releases support trout 'including natural (wild) reproduction' in some TVA tailwaters, but no Hiwassee-specific age-0 survey or agency reproduction statement was found. TU's Hiwassee chapter describes the fishery as stocked (not native). TWRA Region IV reports not verified in this pass.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Cold deep-source tunnel releases sustain the trout reach, but the Reliance gauge hit 23.8 C on 27 July 2025 with 11 days at or above 22 C that month - summer is survivable but marginal in low water.

priorLeads.segment: Holston River MAIN STEM from the North/South Fork confluence at Kingsport through Hawkins, Grainger, Jefferson, and Knox counties to the French Broad confluence at the head of Fort Loudoun Lake (catalog boundaries). The documented trout fact set sits entirely on the Cherokee Dam tailwater sub-reach of this main stem (Jefferson/Grainger counties); South Fork Holston tailwaters and North Fork Holston are separate catalog waters.
priorLeads.boundaries: Kingsport (fork confluence) to French Broad confluence; TWRA's smallmouth exception manages 'I-40 bridge upstream to Cherokee Dam' on this main stem; the stocking program is reach-pinned to 'Cherokee TW / Holston River' (Jefferson/Grainger).

coldSourceSummary.notes: TWRA Trout Management Plan 2017-2027 (Fisheries Report 17-10): 'The Cherokee and Apalachia tailwaters also have summer thermal bottlenecks (with water temperatures >70 F) and receive adult Rainbow and Brown Trout during the fall and spring' — an agency-documented summer thermal ceiling on this tailwater, and a seasonally (not year-round) cold regime. TDEC's 2026 303(d) list records a 26.9-mile Holston River segment in Jefferson County (unit TN06010104001_2000) impaired for DISSOLVED OXYGEN with source 'DAM OR IMPOUNDMENT' (plus FLOW REGIME MODIFICATION, dam-sourced) — the dam-release water-quality signature on the Cherokee-Dam-downstream reach; the 303(d) sheet prints unit IDs and miles but not boundary text, so reach attribution rests on the dam-sourced source field and Jefferson County location. Release draw level (bottom-draw vs epilimnion) is not documented in any source retrieved; TVA's Cherokee page could not be fetched (blocked). Gauge note: USGS 03493510 'HOLSTON RIVER AT CHEROKEE DAM(TW), TN' (Jefferson Co., HUC 06010104, drainage 3,428 sq mi) is a discontinued discrete-sampling site, and no active USGS gauge reports on the Holston main stem in Tennessee.

holdover.detail: No holdover or year-round survival documentation found for the Cherokee tailwater reach. TWRA's own plan designs this as a seasonal fishery: adult trout stocked fall and spring around a documented >70 F summer thermal bottleneck; STMP documents significant natural brown trout reproduction only for the South Holston and Wilbur tailwaters, not Cherokee.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout population documented on the Holston main stem / Cherokee tailwater. The STMP statement that significant natural brown trout reproduction enables wild management applies only to the South Holston and Wilbur tailwaters ('no Brown Trout are stocked' there — unlike Cherokee, which receives adult Browns).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Owner-box conflict, stated both sides: the site feed (repo trout-calendar.json) claims 'No trout program (warmwater fishery)' and the owner-supplied workbook row 'Cherokee TW / Holston River' carries NO stocking months, while the catalog YAML claims a Nov-Apr program and TWRA's LIVE 2026 schedule (fetched 2026-09-18) confirms the row WITH months 'J, F, M, A, N, D' (Rainbow + Brown) — and TWRA's own plan documents >70 F summer thermal bottlenecks on this tailwater, i.e., a documented seasonal fishery rather than documented year-round survival.

priorLeads.segment: Horse Creek, a Greene County Cherokee National Forest tributary running out of the Bald Mountains down to the Nolichucky River; TWRA spring-stocked with a special trout regulation on its national-forest reach.
priorLeads.boundaries: Special trout regulation reach (live-verified on the state's regs publisher): 'Horse Creek: Greene County, U.S. Forest Service Boundary Line upstream to the junction of Squibb Creek.' Stocking workbook rows are undivided 'Horse Creek' (Greene County). Stocking-identity pin: the 2026-09-17 workbook contains NO 'Camp Creek' row for Greene County (its only Camp Creek entry is 'Puncheon Camp Creek', Grainger County) - all 8 weekly rows name 'Horse Creek', so the catalog reach identity is unambiguous. TDEC stations used: TDECWPC-HORSE007.0GE (RM 7.0, Horse Creek Rd - inside the stocked drainage) and TDECWPC-HORSE000.7GE (RM 0.7, near the Nolichucky mouth).

coldSourceSummary.notes: Free-flowing forest creek ('classic bank-and-boulder small water' per catalog); no dam, no spring claim. Neighbor context (different stream, clearly attributed): USGS-03466295 'CAMP CREEK AT CAMP CREEK, TN' (9.99 sq mi, the adjacent Cherokee NF creek in the same Camp Creek community) grabbed 14.0-18.5 C across nine summer days 1984-1988 - the Horse Creek/Camp Creek forest drainage cluster runs cool. Station identities verified via WQP Station metadata (USGS identity endpoint down this week).

holdover.detail: No holdover documentation found; stocking is weekly seasonal (Mar 1 - Jun 7 in the 2026 workbook) with no posted post-stocking persistence data.

wildPopulation.detail: Horse Creek does not appear on the wild-trout-streams list on TWRA's regulations publisher page; the county's wild waters are Paint Creek and Rocky Fork. Horse Creek instead carries its own stocked-fishery special regulation (7 trout/day, dropping to 2/day May 1-Sep 30 above the USFS boundary).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: The only in-reach summer grab ran 19.42 C (RM 7.0, Sept 2007) and the adjacent Camp Creek gauge in the same forest drainage grabbed 14.0-18.5 C across nine summer days 1984-88 - cool headwater habitat - but stocking is spring-only and nothing documents trout persisting past the season.
